buzz-cut: Hair clipped very short and even all over the head with clippers, about 3 mm, following the head shape.
crew-cut: Short tapered sides and back, top slightly longer (about 2-3 cm) and brushed up and forward.
butch-cut: Very short, uniform length all over (about 6 mm), slightly longer than a buzz, rounded neat shape.
ivy-league: A longer crew cut: short tapered sides, top long enough to part on the side and sweep across.
caesar-cut: Short even layers with a short straight horizontal fringe brushed forward onto the forehead.
french-crop: Faded sides, textured top pushed forward into a short blunt fringe across the forehead.
low-fade: Sides fade from skin just above the ears and neckline, getting longer upward; top kept a few centimetres long and neatly styled.
mid-fade: Fade starting at temple height on the sides and back, blending smoothly into a medium-length top.
high-fade: Fade starting high near the top of the head, sides almost shaved, short top.
skin-fade: Sides and back blended down to bare skin with a smooth gradient, longer textured top.
taper-fade: Subtle taper only at the sideburns and neckline, natural length elsewhere, clean edges.
undercut: Sides and back cut very short in one length, top left long and swept back or to the side, sharp contrast.
disconnected-undercut: Shaved sides with a hard visible disconnection line to a long top slicked to one side.
pompadour: Long top swept upward and back with lots of volume at the front, short neat sides, glossy finish.
quiff: Top hair brushed up and slightly back at the front with volume and texture, shorter sides.
slicked-back: Medium-long top combed straight back with a smooth wet-look shine, tidy short sides.
side-part: Classic short haircut with a clean side parting, top combed neatly to one side.
hard-part: Side part with a sharp shaved line cut into the parting, faded sides, top combed over.
faux-hawk: Short sides with the top hair pushed up and toward the centre into a soft ridge.
mohawk: Sides of the head fully shaved, a strip of longer hair standing up along the centre from front to back.
flat-top: Short sides, top hair standing straight up and cut perfectly flat and level on top.
high-and-tight: Military style: sides and back shaved very high and tight, a small patch of short hair on top.
textured-crop: Short faded sides, choppy messy textured top with a short fringe pushed forward.
fringe: Hair brushed forward so a fringe covers the forehead, medium length on top, short sides.
curtains: Medium-length hair parted in the middle, falling on both sides of the forehead like curtains.
bowl-cut: Rounded cut of even length all around as if trimmed around a bowl, straight fringe.
mullet: Short on the front and sides, long at the back down to the neck.
modern-mullet: Faded or short sides, textured top and front, longer flowing hair at the back of the neck.
man-bun: Long hair pulled back and tied into a bun at the back of the head.
top-knot: Shaved or faded sides with the long top hair tied into a small knot on the crown.
long-hair: Hair grown long past the shoulders, natural with soft waves.
surfer-hair: Medium-long, messy, wavy, sun-bleached looking hair, relaxed and tousled.
afro: Natural curly hair grown out into a round full afro shape.
twists: Hair twisted into small rope-like twists all over the top, sides shorter.
dreadlocks: Hair formed into neat locs falling from the top of the head.
cornrows: Hair braided flat to the scalp in straight neat rows from front to back.
box-braids: Hair split into square sections and braided into individual braids.
waves: Very short brushed hair forming 360 degree rippling waves pattern, clean line-up edges.
curly-top: Short faded sides with a defined curly top.
shag: Layered, choppy medium-length cut with feathered ends and volume on top.
bro-flow: Medium-length hair swept back from the forehead, flowing down behind the ears.
brush-up: Top brushed straight up with volume and a natural matte finish, short sides.
spiky: Short hair styled up into sharp separate spikes with gel.
shaved-head: Head shaved completely smooth and bald with a razor.
edgar-cut: Very straight blunt fringe cut in a horizontal line across the forehead, sharp line-up, high skin fade on the sides.
burst-fade: Fade curving around the ear in a semicircle, longer at the back neckline, textured top.
comb-over-fade: Faded sides with the top combed over to one side with a parting.
rockabilly: 1950s style: big greasy pompadour on top, combed-back sides, ducktail at the back.
messy-tousled: Medium-short hair with an intentionally messy, tousled, effortless look.
frohawk: Curly afro hair shaped into a mohawk: tall curly centre strip, short faded sides.
light-stubble: A few days of short even stubble across the jaw, cheeks and upper lip.
heavy-stubble: Dense short stubble about a week long, neatly edged.
short-boxed: Short full beard trimmed close with clean sharp cheek and neck lines.
full-beard: Thick full beard covering jaw, chin and cheeks, connected to the mustache, medium length.
garibaldi: Wide, full natural beard with a rounded bottom, about 15-20 cm long, with a natural mustache.
bandholz: Very long, full, untrimmed beard reaching the chest with a full mustache.
ducktail: Full beard with the chin hair grown longer and shaped to a point, like a duck's tail.
verdi: Short rounded full beard (no longer than 10 cm) with a separate, styled, prominent mustache.
goatee: Hair only on the chin, cheeks and upper lip clean shaven.
circle-beard: Mustache connected to a chin goatee forming a rounded circle around the mouth.
van-dyke: Pointed chin goatee with a separate mustache that does not connect, cheeks clean shaven.
anchor: Pointed beard along the jawline under the chin shaped like an anchor, with a mustache.
balbo: Floating mustache with a chin beard extending under the lower lip, no sideburns.
chin-strap: Thin line of beard following the jawline from ear to ear, no mustache.
chin-curtain: Beard along the jaw and chin hanging down like a curtain, no mustache.
mutton-chops: Thick sideburns extending down the cheeks to the jaw corners, chin and mustache shaved.
friendly-chops: Mutton chops connected to a mustache, chin clean shaven.
sideburns: Long, thick, neat sideburns down to the earlobes or lower, rest of the face clean shaven.
soul-patch: Small patch of hair just below the lower lip, rest of the face clean shaven.
chevron: Thick, wide mustache covering the upper lip, trimmed in a chevron shape, rest shaven.
handlebar: Mustache with long ends curled upward and waxed, rest of the face clean shaven.
walrus: Very thick, bushy mustache drooping over the mouth, rest of the face shaven.
horseshoe: Mustache with vertical extensions down both sides of the mouth to the jaw, like an upside-down U.
pencil: Very thin, narrow, precisely trimmed mustache just above the lip.
fu-manchu: Thin mustache with long ends growing downward past the chin, rest shaven.
imperial: Big mustache with ends swept upward along the cheeks, with sideburns.
dali: Thin mustache with long ends waxed and pointing sharply straight upward.
english: Narrow, long mustache with the ends pulled to the sides and waxed into points.
lumberjack: Big, thick, rugged full beard, slightly untamed, with a full mustache.
hipster: Long full beard, well groomed, combed and shaped, with a styled mustache.
beard-fade: Full beard that fades from skin at the sideburns gradually into a fuller beard on the jaw and chin.
corporate: Short, tidy, well-groomed full beard, about 1 cm, with clean lines.
extended-goatee: Goatee with mustache extending slightly along the jawline, cheeks shaven.
royale: Mustache with a separate rectangular chin strip, no hair on the cheeks.
wizard: Extremely long, flowing full beard, grey or white, reaching far below the chest.
forked: Long full beard split into two points at the bottom.
viking: Long full beard with a braid at the chin, rugged mustache.
spade: Full beard trimmed into a flat-bottomed spade shape with rounded sides.
old-dutch: Long wide beard along the jaw and chin with no mustache.
pointed: Full beard trimmed to a sharp point at the chin.
clean-shaven: All facial hair shaved completely smooth, no beard or mustache.
salt-pepper: Medium full beard with natural mixed grey and dark hairs, salt and pepper colour.
sharp-lineup: Short full beard with very crisp razor-sharp line-up on the cheeks and neck.
hollywoodian: Beard on the jaw and chin connected to a mustache, but no sideburns.
zappa: Thick mustache combined with a soul patch under the lip.
beardstache: Thick prominent mustache with very short stubble on the rest of the face.
painters-brush: Thick, full, wide mustache like a painter's brush, rest of face shaven.
lampshade: Mustache trimmed in a straight-edged trapezoid shape like a lampshade, rest shaven.
red-full: Full medium-length beard in a ginger red colour.
yeard: Full beard grown untrimmed for about a year, long and thick with a big mustache.
